title: United Airlines Flight 232: CRM-positive control under catastrophic hydraulic loss
summary: United 232 is encoded as a positive-control record for the flight-deck state pattern: an extremely degraded aircraft state was not fully recoverable, but crew coordination and outside assistance materially shaped survivability, while underlying design/inspection failures remain separate.

status_history.note: Added to calibrate MKH-PAT-0022 against anti-crew or anti-automation overfit.

claims.claim: The NTSB page identifies United 232 as a July 19, 1989 DC-10 accident after catastrophic No. 2 engine failure caused loss of all three hydraulic systems, producing severe flight-control difficulty and casualties.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The NTSB probable-cause summary attributes the accident to inadequate consideration of human-factors limitations in inspection and quality-control procedures, fan-disk failure from a crack, and engine debris whose energy and trajectories exceeded hydraulic-system protective design.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The FAA Lessons Learned module notes that an off-duty DC-10 check airman assisted the crew; it describes CRM teamwork/assertion and throttle manipulation as central to the crew response, and reports that NTSB called the crew performance highly commendable and indicative of CRM value.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The FAA module records 29 NTSB recommendations and later FAA/industry initiatives, making United 232 both a CRM-positive control and a correction-infusion follow-through surface.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: As a control record, United 232 calibrates MKH-PAT-0022 by showing that flight-deck coordination can be a resilience surface as well as a failure surface; it does not erase the design, inspection, and hydraulic-system vulnerabilities recorded by NTSB.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

evidence_refs.support_type: control role encoded in this record
positive control relation to flight-deck state pattern candidate

evidence_profile.source_depth: one-pass NTSB landing page and FAA Lessons Learned extraction
limitations: Not a full technical monograph on DC-10 hydraulic design or fan-disk metallurgy.
Does not claim CRM alone produced survival or that training can compensate for design common-mode hazards.

type_payload.fit_rationale: United 232 prevents MKH-PAT-0022 from maturing as a one-sided pilot-error or state-confusion pattern: severe physical degradation was partly managed through crew coordination and extra expertise, while inspection/design vulnerabilities remain explicit.
limits: Positive control does not mature MKH-PAT-0022.
Crew performance is not used to excuse design/inspection vulnerabilities.
The record requires full-report and recommendation-closure second pass before stronger synthesis.

handling_notes: Aviation records must preserve the dignity of passengers, crew, families, responders, and survivors.
Do not flatten human-factors findings into pilot blame; separate physical system state, displayed state, automation mode, training, procedures, supervision, fatigue, and investigation/legal status.
This is historical/evidentiary infrastructure, not operational flight-safety guidance or legal advice.

unknowns: Full NTSB report and recommendation-closure details not second-pass extracted.
Survival statistics, cabin/fire/rescue details, and long-term regulatory changes need child records.
next_actions: Second-pass extract NTSB report and FAA Lessons Learned follow-on initiatives.
Add Qantas 32 or British Airways 009 as additional positive controls; add a negative control where flightdeck factors are not causal.
